Currently, we do not have a fully reliable solution to automatically detect the printer body and exact its contour. Because of this, I strongly prefer that the worker manually defines the printer contour by selecting the four corner points during registration. Once these four corners are defined, all vision models (screw hole and rubber hole detection) can be executed only inside this confirmed printer region.

If we rely entirely on deep learning–based contour detection (for example, using a segmentation or contour extraction model), the result may not be accurate due to image noise, lighting variation, and low image quality. Even small contour errors can cause major downstream problems. For example, if the detected contour is loose and includes background or irrelevant areas, that contour may later be used as a template for printer body detection, which would significantly degrade template-matching accuracy and lead to unstable body localization.

Although we have trained a YOLO model, it sometimes produces loose bounding boxes, which is not acceptable for precise contour definition. We are also considering changing the ZIG color; if the color becomes stable and distinguishable, we may be able to use color slicing to estimate the contour position or at least the center of the printer body. In that case, the worker’s involvement could be reduced. However, even then, I still believe the worker should take minimum responsibility, at least by confirming or selecting the four corners of the printer.

The reason for this approach is not only technical accuracy but also responsibility ownership. If everything is fully automated and a small mistake occurs, all responsibility falls on the vision system and the AI model. By involving the worker in defining the printer contour during registration, part of the responsibility is shared and errors become traceable and explainable.

During daily operation—when we update reference images, contour information, and screw/rubber hole positions (once or twice per day)—the worker should also be asked to confirm the current detection results, including bounding box accuracy and ROI positions. This confirmation step adds an additional safety layer to ensure long-term system stability.
